accepted.question_text: Consider the single-input time-optimal control system q˙ = f(q) + u g(q) on a 3-dimensional smooth manifold M, where f and g are a generic pair of C-infinity vector fields, the control u is any measurable function with |u| <= 1, and trajectories are required to connect fixed endpoints in minimum time. Must every time-optimal trajectory for such a generic 3-dimensional system be piecewise smooth, meaning smooth except at finitely many switching points where the optimal control changes its regime?

evidence.quote: A. (f, g) is a generic pair of vector fields. Optimal trajectories cannot be all smooth; are they piecewise smooth?
The question is open for n = 3.

accepted.question_text: For the same generic 3-dimensional single-input time-optimal problem q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1, define sw(q) to be the least integer k such that every time-optimal trajectory contained in a sufficiently small neighborhood of q has at most k switching points, and set sw(q) = infinity if arbitrarily small neighborhoods of q contain time-optimal trajectories with infinitely many switching points. Is sw(q) finite for every point q in M?

evidence.quote: We set sw(q) = ∞ if any neighborhood of q contains a time-optimal trajectory with an infinite number of switching points.
We do not know if sw(q) < ∞ for any q ∈ M.

accepted.question_text: In the generic 3-dimensional time-optimal control problem q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1, is every individual time-optimal trajectory forced to have only finitely many switching points, even if one does not assume a uniform neighborhood-wise bound on the number of switchings?

evidence.quote: We also do not know if a weaker property, the finiteness of the number of switching points for any individual time-optimal trajectory is valid.

accepted.question_text: In higher-dimensional single-input time-optimal control systems q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1, there are examples of extremals with accumulating switching points whose qualitative structure survives small perturbations of the system. Are such extremals actually time-optimal?

evidence.quote: There are very interesting examples of extremals with accumulating switching points whose structure survives small perturbations (see [21, 37]) but nobody knows if these extremals are optimal.

accepted.question_text: Let M be a real analytic manifold and let f and g be real analytic vector fields, not necessarily generic, in the single-input time-optimal system q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1. If two points are connected by some time-optimal trajectory, must there exist a time-optimal trajectory connecting the same endpoints whose set of switching points is at most countable?

evidence.quote: Main open question here is as follows: Given two points connected by a time-optimal trajectory, can we connect them by a time-optimal trajectory with no more than a countable number of switching points?

accepted.question_text: For the same real analytic single-input time-optimal control setting, can one always choose a time-optimal trajectory between two time-optimally connected points whose set of switching points avoids having positive measure?

evidence.quote: We do not know if we can avoid a positive measure set of switching points.

accepted.question_text: Let gamma_0 and gamma_1 be smooth admissible paths of a sub-Riemannian structure on a manifold M with gamma_0(0) = gamma_1(0) = q_0 and with initial tangent vectors at q_0 that are not collinear. Does there always exist an admissible path connecting gamma_0(1) to gamma_1(1) whose length is strictly smaller than the length of the broken path obtained by concatenating gamma_0 and gamma_1?

evidence.quote: A natural open question here is as follows. Let γi : [0, 1] → M be two smooth admissible paths of a sub-Riemannian structure on the manifold M, γ0(0) = γ1(0) = q0, γ˙0(0) ∧ γ˙1(0) 6= 0. Does there exist an admissible path connecting γ0(1) with γ1(1) that is strictly shorter than the concatenation of the curves γ0 and γ1?

accepted.question_text: Fix a point q_0 in a sub-Riemannian manifold and consider the endpoint map from the Hilbert manifold of H^1 admissible paths starting at q_0 to M, sending each path to its endpoint at time 1. Must this endpoint map always have at least one regular value, or equivalently, is it impossible for singular curves issuing from q_0 to fill the whole manifold M?

evidence.quote: The endpoint maps have plenty of regular points but we do not know if they always have regular values.
We can reformulate the question as follows: is it possible that starting from q0 singular curves fill the whole manifold M?

accepted.question_text: In a sub-Riemannian manifold, optimal singular curves starting from a fixed point q_0 are known to fill a nowhere dense subset of the manifold. Can the set filled by such optimal singular curves nevertheless have positive measure?

evidence.quote: Optimal (i. e. length minimizing) singular curves are better controlled; we know that starting from q0 optimal singular curves fill a nowhere dense subset of M (see [2]). An important open question: can they fill a positive measure subset of M?

accepted.question_text: For a generic sub-Riemannian metric on a 3-dimensional Martinet distribution, consider a sub-Riemannian sphere centered at q_0 and a point where the sphere meets an optimal singular curve. What is the C^1-classification, up to germs of C^1-diffeomorphisms of R^3, of the germ of the sphere at such a point?

evidence.quote: An important open question is to find a C1-classification of the germs of spheres at the points of optimal singular curves for generic metrics.

accepted.question_text: For the Engel distribution, namely a rank-2 distribution on R^4 with n_3(q) = 3 and n_4(q) = 4, sub-Riemannian spheres are 3-dimensional hypersurfaces and every point lies on a unique singular curve whose small segments are optimal. What is the corresponding local classification of sphere singularities at points where such optimal singular curves meet the sphere?

evidence.quote: The next step is the Engel distribution, i. e. a rank 2 distribution in R4 such that n3(q) = 3, n4(q) = 4. There is exactly one singular curve through any point and small segments of singular curves are optimal. We repeat our question for this case; the spheres are now 3-dimensional hypersurfaces in R4.

accepted.question_text: Consider a generic pair of smooth vector fields f_0 and f_1 near a point q_0 in R^2 such that f_0(q_0) and f_1(q_0) are collinear, n_2(q_0) = 1, and n_3(q_0) = 2, and define the almost-Riemannian distance S_{q_0}(q) as the minimum time needed to reach q from q_0 along trajectories of q˙ = u_0 f_0(q) + u_1 f_1(q) under the unit-norm constraint on the two control components stated in the paper. What is the C^1-classification of the germ of the distance function S_{q_0} for such generic pairs?

evidence.quote: The question is to find a C1-classification of the germs of distance functions Sq0 for generic pairs of vector fields f0, f1 among the pairs that satisfy conditions n2(q0) = 1, n3(q0) = 2.

accepted.question_text: Let Delta be a vector distribution on a manifold M, and call it singular transitive when any two points of M can be connected by a concatenation of singular curves of Delta. Does singular transitivity force the symmetry group of Delta, meaning the diffeomorphisms Phi of M with Phi_* Delta = Delta, to be a finite-dimensional Lie group?

evidence.quote: We say that a distribution is singular transitive if any two points of M can be connected by a concatination of singular curves. A natural open question is as follows: Is it true that singular transitivity of the distribution implies that its symmetry group is a finite dimensional Lie group?

accepted.question_text: For each n, let mu(n) be the smallest integer m such that an m-times traversed plane convex curve admits arbitrarily small perturbations that become nondegenerate closed curves in R^n, where nondegeneracy means that the velocity, curvature, torsion, and higher Frenet data never degenerate. What is mu(n) for dimensions n > 3?

evidence.quote: Let µ(n) be minimal m such that run m times convex plane curves have regular small perturbations in Rn. We know that µ(2) = 1, µ(3) = 2. An important open problem is to find µ(n) for n > 3.

accepted.question_text: For regular closed curves in R^n equipped with their orthonormal Frenet frames in O(n), is the length of the Frenet frame always strictly greater than mu(n) times the length of the standard closed geodesic SO(2) embedded in O(n), where mu(n) is the minimum multiplicity needed for a plane convex curve to admit a regular perturbation in R^n?

evidence.quote: An important open problem is to find µ(n) for n > 3 and to check if the length of the Frenet frame of any regular curve in Rn is greater than the length of SO(2) ⊂ O(n) multiplied by µ(n).

accepted.question_text: Consider the incompressible Navier-Stokes equation on the torus with periodic boundary conditions, viewed as a control system on the space V of divergence-free H^1 vector fields, where the forcing eta(t, .) is constrained to lie in a finite-dimensional subspace E of the space of divergence-free fields supported in a fixed open subset D of the torus, and E is required not to depend on the viscosity nu. Is the system approximately controllable in any time under such a localized degenerate forcing?

evidence.quote: Now an important open question: is the system approximately controllable and (or) controllable in the finite dimensional projections by a localized degenerate forcing when E is a finite dimensional subspace of the space {u ∈ V : supp u ⊂ D}¯ ?
The question is about existence and effective construction of such a space E that does not depend on the viscosity ν.

accepted.question_text: In the same Navier-Stokes control setting on the torus, with forcing constrained to a finite-dimensional subspace E of divergence-free vector fields supported in a fixed open set D and chosen independently of the viscosity nu, is the system controllable in finite-dimensional projections in any time?

evidence.quote: Now an important open question: is the system approximately controllable and (or) controllable in the finite dimensional projections by a localized degenerate forcing when E is a finite dimensional subspace of the space {u ∈ V : supp u ⊂ D}¯ ?
The question is about existence and effective construction of such a space E that does not depend on the viscosity ν.

needs_review.question_text_raw: The final section on diffusion along the Reeb field proposes discrete and continuous evolutions of sub-Riemannian metrics and says there is 'a good chance' to obtain a nonzero limiting Hamiltonian by a clever choice of scaling and averaging parameters, but it does not formulate a single precise open question with explicit success criteria.

evidence.quote: To conclude, I would like to discuss one more problem; it is less precise than already stated questions but, to my taste, is nice and fascinating.
There is a good chance to arrive to a nonzero limiting Hamiltonian h∞ by a clever choice of the sequences of positive functions εn, cn.
